planting.note: Set plugs out in spring in fast-draining soil; in colder zones get plants in by mid-summer so they establish before winter.

directions: This ground-hugging ice plant forms a mat of fleshy, finger-like leaves studded with bright yellow, white-eyed flowers from April into June. It wants sharp drainage and full sun, and once rooted in it shrugs off drought with little care. Keep it out of soggy winter soil, since rot rather than cold is usually what kills it. Use it as a sun-baked groundcover or spiller at the edge of a rock garden or dry wall.

planting.note: Plant into gravelly or sandy well-drained soil in spring; avoid heavy, wet ground where the succulent foliage can rot.

directions: Part of the FLASHMOB ice plant series, Action Shot was selected for improved cold hardiness paired with unusually large flowers over evergreen succulent foliage. It spreads into a low, wide mat that handles dry, gravelly sites and hot, sunny exposures better than most groundcovers. Because it stays evergreen in milder climates it can offer some winter interest where hardy. Grow it in lean, sharply drained soil and resist the urge to overwater or over-fertilize.

planting.note: Set out in spring into well-drained, lean soil; performs well in containers as well as rock gardens and border edges.

directions: Ocean Sunset Violet carries unusually large violet-toned blooms in high numbers over a tidy, spreading succulent mound, with flowers that close at night and reopen as the sun climbs. It handles heat and dry spells with ease once rooted, making it a reliable choice for rock gardens, raised beds, or sunny container plantings. Give it full sun and soil that drains quickly, since wet feet are its main vulnerability. It is also deer resistant and holds up well through summer heat.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; give it room toward the back of a border since it grows notably tall for the genus.

directions: Purple Leia sends up tall, columnar spikes densely packed with rosy-purple flowers across the top half of the plant, giving strong vertical structure to mid-border plantings. It tolerates most well-drained soils and even partial shade, though bloom is heaviest with a full day of sun. This selection adds noticeably more height than typical spike speedwells, so pair it with companions that can stand beside rather than in front of it. Deadheading spent spikes can encourage additional flowering into late summer.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil in a sunny border; benefits from a tidy, well-branched habit that needs little staking.

directions: This speedwell produces intensely purple flower spikes over dark green foliage on a well-branched, mounded plant, extending bloom from late spring into late summer. It stays notably clean and disease-free through the season and draws hummingbirds along with bees. Plant in full sun and average, well-drained soil, and divide every few years to keep the clump vigorous. This is a distinct Veronica introduction and should not be confused with a same-named Tulbaghia cultivar sold under a different brand.

planting.note: Set out in spring into well-drained soil; thrives as both a landscape groundcover and a container plant in hot, humid regions.

directions: Jagger is an early-flowering member of the Paparazzi phlox collection, chosen for its strong heat and humidity tolerance, which keeps it looking fresh in both pots and garden beds through summer. It spreads into a low, ground-covering mat that draws bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds while flowering from spring into summer. Plant in full sun with consistent moisture during establishment, then let it fill in as a durable edging or front-of-border plant. Its wide hardiness range suits both warmer and cooler climates better than many creeping phlox types.

planting.note: Transplant in early spring into well-drained soil; monthly feeding helps establish the low, needle-leaved mat quickly.

directions: Violet Pinwheels forms a low, needle-textured mound of dark green foliage covered in vivid purple flowers whose petals are notched and slightly upturned, giving each bloom a pinwheel look. It flowers earliest in the Phlox season, opening in early spring before many border perennials wake up. Give it full sun and well-drained soil, and feed monthly through the growing season for the densest flowering mat. It works well tumbling over rock walls or edging a sunny path.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; self-branching habit needs little pinching to stay full.

directions: Golden Stardust covers itself in small, star-shaped golden-yellow flowers over a long season, branching on its own to form a full, upright clump without pinching. It shows notably better resistance to powdery mildew than many older tickseeds, which keeps the foliage looking cleaner through humid summers. Grow it in full sun and well-drained soil, where it handles heat well and needs only modest watering once established. Shear lightly after the first flush to encourage continued rebloom.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; bulks up quickly in both containers and garden beds.

directions: Sunfetti Yellow Bicolor produces masses of small flowers combining yellow and deep red petals around orange centers, blooming heavily through most of summer on a mounded, well-filled plant. It fills out its space faster than many tickseed types and carries notably better resistance to powdery mildew. Plant in full sun with well-drained soil and expect strong heat tolerance and steady pollinator visits through the season. Its fast bulking habit makes it a good choice where quick coverage is wanted.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; fertilize only as needed since it is a naturally low-maintenance bloomer.

directions: Sunshine Freak! opens with cheerful, light yellow daisy flowers that gradually fade from cream-yellow to white as they age, so a single plant can show several color stages on the same clump at once. It stays low and wide relative to its spread, forming a dense mound rather than a tall upright plant. Grow it in full sun and well-drained soil, where it tolerates heat and drought with minimal feeding. The long bloom season runs from spring well into fall, giving extended color for little upkeep.

common_name: Make My Daisy Happy Shasta Daisy

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; flowers reliably in its first year without needing a cold-vernalization period.

directions: Make My Daisy Happy produces clean, pure white single flowers in heavy coverage over a mounded clump, blooming in its first season without requiring a winter chill to initiate flowers. New flushes of bloom continue through late spring and summer, giving a long display window from a single planting. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil and even moisture while it establishes. It is a reliably uniform choice where a classic white Shasta daisy look is wanted without a wait for the second year.

common_name: Make My Daisy Crazy Shasta Daisy

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; flowers in its first year without needing a cold-vernalization period.

directions: Make My Daisy Crazy shares the clean white color and heavy coverage of its Make My Daisy series relatives but carries semi-double flowers with extra petals for a fuller-looking bloom. It flowers in the first year without a cold period and continues pushing new flowers through the season. Grow it in full sun and well-drained soil, keeping it evenly watered while young. It suits gardeners who want the classic Shasta daisy look with a slightly showier, fuller flower form.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; grassy foliage looks tidy even when the plant is not in flower.

directions: Glowstick sends up bright yellow, nectar-rich flower spikes from summer into fall that draw bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds in steady numbers. When it is not flowering, its finely textured, grass-like foliage still reads as an attractive clump rather than bare stems. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil, where it tolerates both heat and drought once established. Its long bloom window, stretching from midsummer well into fall, gives more weeks of color than many torch lilies.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; part of a breeding line that blooms far longer than traditional thrift.

directions: Dream Clouds is a pure white-flowered member of the Dreameria series, which extends Armeria's bloom well past the traditional short early-spring-and-fall window into a season-long display. Large flowers sit on sturdy stems above a tidy, compact mound of narrow foliage, making it suited to both garden beds and patio containers. Plant in full sun with well-drained soil, where it tolerates heat and resists deer browsing. Its neat habit keeps it looking tidy without regular grooming through the growing season.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; propagates readily from cuttings for growers wanting to bulk up stock.

directions: Daydream carries bright pink blooms on sturdy stems throughout the growing season, part of a Dreameria breeding line that pushes Armeria beyond its usual brief spring-and-fall bloom into a much longer display. The plant keeps a tidy, compact form that suits both landscape plantings and containers, and it resists deer while drawing butterflies. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil, where it tolerates heat well and stays frost hardy through winter. Its narrow grassy foliage stays attractive even between flushes of bloom.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; give it room to spread since it fills out wider than tall.

directions: Amethyst Dream opens from unusual shingled buds into radiant, royal-purple cornflower blooms held above softly haired, silvery foliage. The silver leaves give it strong heat and drought tolerance, letting it hold up in dry summer conditions that can wilt other perennial cornflowers. It spreads wider than it grows tall, so allow generous room between plants in a sunny border. Keep soil well-drained and skip heavy feeding, since this selection performs best without rich, wet growing conditions.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into dry, well-drained soil; needs little to no supplemental fertilizer once established.

directions: Prime Time blooms earlier in the season than many Russian sages, with blue flowers held in dusky purple calyxes. Once the flowers themselves fade, those colorful calyxes persist well into fall, so the plant keeps looking like it is still flowering long after bloom has technically ended. It attracts bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds while standing up well to heat, drought, and deer pressure. Grow it in full sun in dry to average, well-drained soil, and avoid routine fertilizing, which can make the airy, upright habit floppy.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; compact mounding habit needs little staking or deadheading.

directions: Guapa Flamenco Bicolor carries burgundy-centered flowers ringed by bright golden-yellow petal tips, held on a compact, mounded plant that stays tidy without a lot of grooming. It blooms from late spring through fall, giving a long season of color for a relatively small footprint. Grow it in full sun and well-drained soil, where it tolerates heat well and draws pollinators steadily. Its dense habit makes it a good fit for borders or containers where a sprawling blanket flower would be too much.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; compact mounding habit needs little staking or deadheading.

directions: Guapa Red produces red petals surrounding deep red and golden-yellow bicolor centers on a compact, mounding plant that holds its shape without flopping open. Like its Guapa series relatives, it blooms from late spring into fall and tolerates summer heat without slowing down. Grow it in full sun and well-drained soil, and expect fairly low maintenance once it is established. Its tighter habit suits smaller borders and containers better than older, looser blanket flower types.

planting.note: Transplant in fall for winter and spring color in mild climates, or in spring further north; a period of cool weather improves flower quality and habit.

directions: Brightside Bright Yellow is a compact, bushy wallflower covered in vivid yellow bicolor flowers over lush foliage, blooming in its first year and continuing through spring and, in mild climates, into winter. Exposure to a period of cool weather improves both flower color and overall habit compared with unvernalized plants. In the South it can behave as a short-lived perennial, while in colder regions it works well as a cool-season container or bedding plant. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil, where it tolerates drought and resists deer and rabbits.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; deadhead spent spikes to encourage a second flush of bloom.

directions: Bumblesnow is a petite, pure white-flowered sage that rebounds with a strong second bloom when deadheaded after its first flush in late spring and summer. Its compact size keeps it in scale with smaller borders and containers rather than towering over companions. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil and moderate, regular watering for the best flowering performance. It draws hummingbirds and resists deer browsing, making it a dependable small-scale accent plant.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil at the front of a border; a compact habit keeps it from overrunning neighbors.

directions: Bumbleblue produces abundant violet-blue flower spikes over a compact, bushy clump of fragrant, rich green foliage, blooming heavily in late spring and summer. Its small scale suits border fronts and quart-sized container plantings where a larger sage would crowd its neighbors. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil, where it tolerates heat and drought once established. It draws bees in large numbers and resists deer browsing, making it a reliable pollinator plant for small spaces.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; reblooms without needing a cold-vernalization period, tolerating wet conditions better than most dianthus.

directions: Silver Strike pairs bright bicolor pink flowers with silvery-gray foliage on a neat, mounded plant that reblooms consistently from early spring until fall without needing a chilling period. It handles wet spring weather better than many dianthus, which can otherwise struggle with crown rot in rainy conditions. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil and light watering once it is established. Its compact, tidy habit suits landscape borders as well as 2.5-quart and 1-gallon container production.

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil; reblooms without needing a cold-vernalization period, tolerating wet conditions better than most dianthus.

directions: Ruby Snow pairs silvery-gray foliage with white flowers marked by a red eye, holding its color well even under heat and strong sun. Like its Mountain Frost series relatives, it reblooms from early spring until fall without needing a cold period and tolerates wet spring weather better than typical dianthus. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil and only light supplemental watering. Its compact, mounded form fits neatly into landscape borders or container plantings from 2.5-quart to 1-gallon pots.
